lessons.title: もうける (mōkeru) — to make a profit

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Japanese for to be saved up, then the Japanese for to keep down.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: もうける

segments.text: もうける — mōkeru — "to make a profit".
よく うれたら、みせは もうけるでしょう。 — yoku uretara, mise wa mōkeru deshō — "If it sells well, the shop will make a profit."
Polite もうけます, mōkemasu; an ichidan verb. Past (polite): みせが もうけました。, mise ga mōkemashita.

もうける (mōkeru) is a native Japanese word (wago), inherited rather than borrowed from Chinese, and its older origin is not settled. Its kanji was attached to it later as a kun'yomi, a native reading given to a Chinese character (JMdict, KANJIDIC2).
One more word for saying what happens if.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: もうかる

segments.text: もうかる — mōkaru — "to be profitable; to pay".
みせが もうかったら、てんいんを ふやします。 — mise ga mōkattara, ten'in o fuyashimasu — "If the shop does well, we will take on more people."
Polite もうかります, mōkarimasu; a godan verb. Past (polite): みせが もうかりました。, mise ga mōkarimashita.

もうかる (mōkaru) is a native Japanese word (wago), inherited rather than borrowed from Chinese, and its older origin is not settled. Its kanji was attached to it later as a kun'yomi, a native reading given to a Chinese character (JMdict, KANJIDIC2).

blocks.title: You'll want to know: りえき

segments.text: りえき — rieki — "a profit; gains".
りえきが あったら、みんなで わけます。 — rieki ga attara, minna de wakemasu — "If there is a profit, we share it among us."

りえき (rieki) is Sino-Japanese (kango): two Chinese characters read with their on'yomi, readings borrowed from Chinese. They are ri, "advantage" (Middle Chinese lijH) and eki, "benefit" ('jiek) (KANJIDIC2; Middle Chinese in Baxter's transcription).
One more word for saying what happens if.

segments.text: そん — son — "a loss; a disadvantage".
いま うったら、そんを するでしょう。 — ima uttara, son o suru deshō — "If you sell now, you will probably make a loss."

そん (son) is Sino-Japanese (kango): one Chinese character read with its on'yomi, reading borrowed from Chinese. It is son, "loss" (Middle Chinese swonX) (KANJIDIC2; Middle Chinese in Baxter's transcription).
One more word for saying what happens if.

lessons.gloss: to go out of business; to be crushed

blocks.title: You'll want to know: つぶれる

segments.text: つぶれる — tsubureru — "to go out of business; to be crushed".
きゃくが すくなく なったら、みせは つぶれるでしょう。 — kyaku ga sukunaku nattara, mise wa tsubureru deshō — "If the customers fall away, the shop will probably go under."
Polite つぶれます, tsuburemasu; an ichidan verb. Past (polite): みせが つぶれました。, mise ga tsuburemashita.

つぶれる (tsubureru) is a native Japanese word (wago), inherited rather than borrowed from Chinese, and its older origin is not settled. Its kanji was attached to it later as a kun'yomi, a native reading given to a Chinese character (JMdict, KANJIDIC2).
One more word for saying what happens if.
